stories.title: Smith County launches law enforcement mental health program
stories.summary: Smith County is launching a proactive mental health program for law enforcement. The initiative follows testimony from a retired officer who described the long-term impact of responding to traumatic calls. The program aims to provide support before officers reach a point of crisis.

stories.title: Foundation 2 Crisis Services names new CEO
stories.summary: Foundation 2 Crisis Services, a mental health nonprofit and 988 provider, has appointed Erin Langdon as its new CEO. Langdon, who has been aware of the organization since her youth, takes over a service that has operated a 24/7 crisis support line since 1970.

stories.title: Therapist outlines boundary setting for mental health
stories.summary: Licensed therapist Cynthia Piccini suggests that setting boundaries is essential for maintaining personal peace and energy. Piccini advises that individuals should define clear limits on their time and capacity, particularly if they consistently feel depleted after interacting with specific people or situations.

stories.title: Construction industry holds inaugural mental health summit
stories.summary: The United Association and the Mechanical Contractors Association of America held a joint summit in Washington, D.C. to address mental health in construction. The event focused on translating awareness into practical workplace programs for contractors and labor leaders to implement across their organizations.

stories.summary: Shoppers at participating Americana Manhasset businesses can direct 25 percent of eligible purchases to the Seleni Institute from December 3 to December 5, 2026. The organization provides mental health care for women and families. The donation requires shoppers to register and designate the institute.

stories.title: Oklahoma Children’s OU Health opens behavioral center
stories.summary: Oklahoma Children’s OU Health has opened a comprehensive pediatric behavioral health center in Oklahoma City. The facility integrates inpatient and outpatient services, including 72 beds for children and adolescents. It is the first center of its kind in the state to be integrated with a children’s hospital.

stories.title: Survey reports high mental health burden in rare disease community
stories.summary: A Rare Barometer survey of nearly 500 people found that seven in 10 individuals affected by rare diseases report poor mental health. Nearly half experienced symptoms of depression at rates six times higher than the general UK population. Isolation was also reported as significantly more common.

stories.title: CSUSB addresses racial trauma in student mental health
stories.summary: Cal State San Bernardino is focusing on the specific mental health needs of Black students facing systemic racism and trauma. The university is working to ensure counseling services account for the weight of these experiences, which have been exacerbated by national events and longstanding healthcare disparities.

stories.title: IIT Delhi announces mental health policy reforms
stories.summary: IIT Delhi will hire more counselors and mandate mental health sensitization workshops for faculty and staff. These reforms follow an external inquiry into the death of a student in August 2026. The institute aims to strengthen student welfare through these institutional policy changes.

stories.summary: Research indicates that consistent meditation may lead to modest improvements in blood pressure by reducing stress and slowing breathing. Experts note that meditation should be used alongside, not instead of, medication and other heart-healthy habits. It is presented as a potential tool for managing hypertension.

Researchers followed nearly 200 adults over eight weeks, finding that those who slept earlier tended to lose more weight. Sleep timing is now being positioned as a potential health target.

stories.title: Sleep coaching shows limited impact on blood sugar
stories.summary: A randomized controlled trial led by NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing found that while sleep coaching helped participants feel less sleepy, it did not change blood sugar levels. The study suggests sleep timing remains a promising target for weight loss, though its metabolic effects require further investigation.

stories.title: Supine sleep does not increase apnea in newborns
stories.summary: A study of 261 neonates in the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine suggests that lying on the back does not worsen sleep apnea in newborns. While supine sleep is known to increase apnea in adults, the findings indicate the current medical recommendation for infants remains appropriate.

stories.summary: Investigators from Mass General Brigham report that pulse oximeters may undercount breathing events in Black patients, potentially leading to inaccurate severity classifications. Researchers found that oxygen-desaturation events were 20 percent lower in Black participants than white participants. The technology is used to define clinical severity.

stories.title: Stair climbers and fitness claims
stories.summary: Proponents of the stair climber claim the machine boosts cardiovascular fitness, strength and bone health. Research shows it offers specific benefits, though it does not always outperform other forms of cardio. The machine is currently enjoying a surge in popularity on social media.

stories.title: Returning to exercise after injury
stories.summary: Surgeons advise against resuming previous exercise intensity immediately after a long break or injury to avoid placing extra stress on the knees. Gradual reintroduction is recommended to prevent further damage. An active lifestyle remains the goal, provided one watches for warning signs.

stories.title: Scientists identify potential muscle repair protein
stories.summary: Researchers at Kyushu University have discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle-repair protein into a version dubbed Super HGF. Early experiments in mice suggest this could help combat age-related muscle loss and strength decline. The protein is currently protected from chemical damage.

stories.title: Nutrient gaps in plant-based diets
stories.summary: A study of 3,500 people suggests replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives may lead to micronutrient deficiencies, particularly in women, teenagers and children. Researchers suggest mandatory fortification of these products and other foods like bread could help. The study used a novel modelling technique.

stories.title: Kenya reports improvements in women's health
stories.summary: Kenya recorded 91 per cent of births in health facilities and 92 per cent with skilled assistance in the 2025-26 survey. Maternal mortality for women aged 15 to 50 dropped to 66 per 1,000. Teenage pregnancy currently stands at 11.9 per cent.

stories.title: Medical attention for pica cravings
stories.summary: Pica involves persistent cravings for non-food items like chalk or soil. While often viewed as a psychological issue, it is frequently linked to iron deficiency and other medical conditions. The condition affects children and adults, with risks dependent on the specific items consumed.

stories.title: Carbohydrates and biological age
stories.summary: A study of 104 Australians aged 65 to 75 suggests higher-carbohydrate diets may be associated with a lower biological age. Researchers note that complex carbohydrates support metabolism and cognitive function. The findings were published in the journal Aging Cell.

stories.title: Dairy alternatives and nutrient intake
stories.summary: Experts writing in the Lancet Planetary Health journal suggest that swapping dairy for plant-based alternatives like oat or almond milk may lead to vitamin and mineral deficiencies. Children, teenagers and women are identified as the groups most affected by these dietary shifts.

stories.title: Decoding fruit juice labels
stories.summary: Consumers often assume fruit juice, fruit drinks and 100 per cent juice offer identical nutritional benefits. Experts note these products differ significantly in sugar composition and fruit content. Understanding labels is recommended to ensure informed purchasing decisions.

stories.title: Greek yoghurt versus Indian curd
stories.summary: Greek yoghurt is frequently marketed as a high-protein alternative to traditional curd. Nutritionists suggest checking labels for protein and sugar content before assuming the more expensive product is the smarter choice. Marketing often highlights the protein content of the thicker variety.

stories.title: Vitamin C and infant development
stories.summary: Research from Oregon Health and Science University suggests higher vitamin C intake during pregnancy may support infant emotional well-being. The study found that mothers with high stress levels often had lower vitamin C intake. Supplemental vitamin C is described as a low-cost intervention.

stories.title: School lunchbox nutritional gaps
stories.summary: A study of 126 Hyderabad school children found a lack of dietary diversity in packed lunches, with cereals dominating. Researchers highlight an urgent need for nutritional education and lunch standards to address the dual burden of malnutrition in children.

stories.title: Dubai's healthy ageing initiative
stories.summary: Dubai aims to become a global hub for healthy ageing by focusing on preventive healthcare and early disease detection. Experts suggest that current infrastructure and government initiatives are key to helping residents live longer. The city is preparing for the Next-Gen Medicine event.

stories.title: Habits for brain health after 60
stories.summary: Research suggests that consistent choices regarding diet, movement and social connections support cognitive health in older age. Experts recommend leafy greens, beans and berries alongside regular sleep. Living longer is described as only part of the goal for healthy ageing.

stories.title: Mainstream interest in longevity
stories.summary: A 2025 McKinsey survey indicates that 60 per cent of consumers consider healthy ageing a top priority. Longevity has shifted from niche biohacking communities into mainstream wellness. Consumers are increasingly seeking practical ways to preserve cognitive function and mobility over time.

stories.title: BriarPatch Co-op to host winter wellness workshop
stories.summary: The BriarPatch Food Co-op is hosting a workshop on November 12, 2026, to teach Ayurvedic methods for winter health. Practitioner Jess Hartley will discuss food and lifestyle choices intended to support immunity and digestion. The session covers concepts like Agni and Ojas for seasonal balance.

stories.title: Creatine HCl study explores brain injury outcomes in mice
stories.summary: US supplement brand CON-CRĒT announced preclinical research on the neuroprotective effects of creatine hydrochloride following traumatic brain injury. Researchers at the University of Nebraska Medical Center found improved markers of neuronal health in mice receiving the supplement. The study has been submitted for publication.

stories.title: Greenspace Herbs launches quantum-enhanced curcumin
stories.summary: Greenspace Herbs has launched Curcumin QA, a product using proprietary EASI technology and a platform called Quantum Ayurveda. The company claims the product applies principles of quantum physics and AI to re-engineer how herbal actives behave in the body. It is designed for higher absorption at lower doses.

stories.title: Representatives seek medical care for Asaram Bapu
stories.summary: Representatives for 87-year-old Asaram Bapu have requested improved medical facilities and Ayurvedic treatment at Jodhpur Central Jail. Citing multiple serious health complications, his team is seeking regular cardiac monitoring and supervision for the prisoner. The request follows concerns raised by his legal representatives regarding his current condition.

stories.title: Kerala opens applications for postgraduate Ayurveda courses
stories.summary: The Commissioner for Entrance Examinations in Kerala has opened the application process for postgraduate MD and MS Ayurveda courses. Candidates who cleared the NEET PG entrance are eligible to apply for government and private colleges. The deadline for option registration is November 10, 2026.

stories.title: Kerala reopens applications for undergraduate AYUSH courses
stories.summary: The Commissioner for Entrance Examinations in Kerala has reopened online applications for undergraduate Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Siddha, and Unani courses. Eligible candidates may submit applications before the Stray Vacancy Round 1. The final date for submission is November 7, 2026.

stories.title: Herbal Kumbh event begins in Uttarakhand
stories.summary: A three-day event titled Herbal Kumbh Jadi-Buti Mela and Dhanvantri Mahotsav 2026 has commenced in Pauri Garhwal. Patanjali University Chancellor Acharya Balkrishna stated the site will become a global centre for herbal medicines, Ayurveda, and spiritual tourism. He expects the location's popularity to echo worldwide within five years.

stories.title: Guide to evidence-based wellness options
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. This guide from NTNU provides an overview of evidence-based options for everyday wellness, focusing on the use of herbal supplements and related practices. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Open merit candidates secure minority of postgraduate Ayurveda spots
stories.summary: The provisional merit list for postgraduate Ayurveda courses in Jammu and Kashmir shows open merit candidates occupying 49 of 113 available positions. Reserved category candidates hold the remaining 64 spots. Within the top 10 rankings, open merit candidates secured three positions.

stories.title: Patient reports arthritis relief from drug-free therapy
stories.summary: A 67-year-old patient reports that a drug-free therapy helped manage osteoarthritis symptoms and avoid joint replacement surgery. The patient, who was diagnosed in 2022, credits the approach with allowing her to reduce painkiller use. The report describes her experience with managing wear-and-tear arthritis through non-surgical means.

stories.title: Ayla Wolf discusses career in functional neurology
stories.summary: Ayla Wolf, founder of Healing Response Acupuncture and Functional Neurology, describes her career path from childhood interest in herbal potions to professional study. She highlights her background in the biochemistry of herbs and the science behind vitamin properties, alongside her work in functional neurology.

stories.title: Ayurvedic practices suggested for winter health
stories.summary: Ayurvedic seasonal practices, known as Ritucharya, suggest adjusting food habits and daily routines to manage winter-related dryness and fatigue. The approach focuses on warmth and nourishment to maintain balance as temperatures drop. These methods are presented as simple ways to support well-being during seasonal changes.
